what: A one-screen panel is held for as many screens as there are scenes. For each scene, over 1 share it zooms to 2.4x as if rushing past the camera (power1.in), disappearing over .65 after .1, while the next scene comes in from .88x into place over .8 after .2 (sine.inOut). It follows with scrub .6, and when scrolling stops it snaps to the nearest scene position in 1.2s. The head text disappears in the last .6 share

options.step: Number of screens used per scene, default 1 — original phone is .65
options.zoom: Scale the outgoing scene grows to, default 2.4
options.from: Starting scale of the entering scene, default .88
options.out-at · out-dur: Fade-out start · length (share of scene), default .1 · .65 — phone .05 · .45
options.in-at · in-dur: Next scene entrance start · length, default .2 · .8 — phone .15 · .55
options.snap: Length in seconds for settling into the scene position after stopping, default 1.2 — 0 means no settling
options.[data-fx-part=scene]: Scenes to stack (two or more) — layout inside is up to the consumer

use: <section data-fx="scene-zoom-pin"><header data-fx-part="head">Your small title here</header><article data-fx-part="scene">…</article><article data-fx-part="scene">…</article></section>
note: In the original, before the pin, while the section’s top edge travels from 85% of the screen to the top, the two words of the first scene gather from ±12% and the photo rises from 60px below — that is tied to in-scene layout, so it lives only in the site’s index.js

from.where: index.html .experiences__stage — original Experiences (four scenes of ‹Secret | photo | Coves›, desktop step 1, phone .65)
